components: Introduction to Business and Consumer Studies
Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Business and Consumer Perspectives on Food Quality
Study food quality from business, consumer and food-science perspectives. General and laboratory safety requirements carry no credits and precede relevant practical work.
Quantitative and Qualitative Research Techniques in the Social Sciences
Food Innovation Research, a Gamma-Beta Approach
Selected restricted finance course: Financial Management in Agriculture. Corporate Financial Management is the other listed option.

Selected restricted methods course: Decision Science 2. The handbook recommends this option for a Business Economics or Operations Research thesis. Methods selection depends on the thesis topic and must be agreed with the thesis coordinator.
Selected restricted strategy course: Strategic Change Management and Innovation. Supply Chain Design and Planning is the other listed option.

The current handbook requires 102 credits of compulsory and restricted study, including all first-year courses. The twelve credits include a one-credit Bachelor Assessment, which must be passed before the eleven-credit individual thesis. The module refers to a course guide for further required knowledge; its current chair-specific conditions remain unverified.
Thirty credits remain open for a minor, an individual minor or elective courses.

routeSelection.basis: Generic target has two parallel majors with no general route. The current handbook lists Spec. A Business Studies before Consumer Studies; retain that neutral order independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Business strategy, markets & decision methods
alternatives.concept: Study firms, markets, strategy, accounting and international business alongside product design and organisational behaviour. Use empirical research, data analysis, econometrics, optimisation and decisions under uncertainty to examine business choices and innovation.
alternatives.labelReason: Describes the actual completed study priorities; no dedicated supply-chain, sensory-science or professional equivalence claim.
progression: All current planned offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Foundations precede dependent business, research and quantitative courses; introductory data precedes machine learning. Some psychology and marketing are concurrent under their actual open formal rules.

alternatives.label: Consumer behaviour, marketing & product insight
alternatives.concept: Combine consumer psychology, behavioural economics, marketing, product design and persuasion with market research and qualitative and quantitative methods. Examine how choices, social influence and customer needs shape products, communication and responsible business decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: Describes the actual completed study priorities; no dedicated supply-chain, sensory-science or professional equivalence claim.
progression: All current planned offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Foundations precede dependent business, research and quantitative courses; introductory data precedes machine learning. Some psychology and marketing are concurrent under their actual open formal rules.
alternatives.distinctness: Changes academic priorities to consumer choice, social influence, qualitative inquiry and persuasion rather than optimisation and institutional business study. Pairwise unique-course counts: 5. These are consequences of the concepts, not arbitrary floor substitutions.

alternatives.label: Sustainable & circular business transformation
alternatives.concept: Combine business strategy, marketing, product design and economics with life-cycle assessment, climate evidence and sustainability governance. Study organisational change, responsibility and circular products through consumer research and the social conditions of sustainable production and consumption.
alternatives.labelReason: Describes the actual completed study priorities; no dedicated supply-chain, sensory-science or professional equivalence claim.
progression: All current planned offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Foundations precede dependent business, research and quantitative courses; introductory data precedes machine learning. Some psychology and marketing are concurrent under their actual open formal rules.
alternatives.distinctness: Changes academic priorities to life-cycle evaluation, circular product design, climate, justice and governance rather than the quantitative or consumer-insight emphasis. Pairwise unique-course counts: 9, 10. These are consequences of the concepts, not arbitrary floor substitutions.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Management, marketing, strategy, organisation and innovation across firms and value chains
Economics, accounting, finance and quantitative decision analysis
Research methods, statistics, data and information technology for business evidence
Business-specialisation depth in management, accounting, supply chains, finance and agribusiness
Professional practice, collaboration, communication and independent research
adjacent: Consumer behaviour, psychology, marketing, product development and communication
Sustainable and circular business, responsible consumption and corporate responsibility
Business intelligence, market data and digital transformation
questions: How can organisations align strategy, operations and supply chains with market and consumer needs?
Why do consumers choose particular products, and how can marketing and design create responsible value?
How can data and sustainability evidence guide innovation and circular business models?

trace: Mandatory academic research literacy, reflective collaboration and professional development.
Costing, budgeting, reporting, performance and discounted investment appraisal directly support business accounting and finance.
AI applications in firms, innovation, productivity, labour and corporate governance support organisational technology decisions, not programming competence.
Contracts, trade, transport transactions, intellectual property and e-commerce compliance supply concrete cross-border commercial-law content.
Financial markets, instruments, banking risk and a simulated bank provide financial-system analysis; not farm accounting or full corporate-finance equivalence.
Production, costs, consumer choice, markets and algebraic/graphical economic analysis support business-economic reasoning.
International macroeconomic markets, growth, expectations and policy provide a bounded external business-environment complement.
Choice under uncertainty, strategic interaction, imperfect competition and allocation implement microeconomic and behavioural analysis.
Externalities, efficiency/equity, taxation and evaluated policy evidence explain institutional conditions of responsible markets.
Description-supported OLS/GLS/IV, tests, Monte Carlo simulation and an empirical paper implement econometric evidence.
Description-supported biases, heuristics, framing and experiments supply behavioural-economic choice analysis.
Customer interviews, specifications, concepts, prototypes, production plans and environmental effects directly develop consumer-oriented products.
Consumer psychology, brand strategy, primary/secondary evidence and customer-journey analysis directly develop marketing and consumer engagement.
Description-supported strategic plans, digital opportunities, business models and responsible transformation implement business strategy.
Description-supported planning and execution of customer research and reporting supply market evidence; no undocumented advanced methods invented.
Trade, foreign investment, governance, responsibility and researched market-entry strategies support international firm decisions.
Startup concepts, customer needs, business models, operations, finance and an investor pitch provide integrated business foundations.
Research questions, measurement, sampling, designs, R statistics and an executed group study provide empirical methods.
Emotional labour, inclusion and psychological safety support organisational leadership; an original survey builds workplace-research skills.
Motivation, teams, power, culture, structure, change and a systematic review directly support organisational behaviour.
Bargaining, BATNA, value creation, power and simulations develop negotiation in stakeholder and business decisions.
Bayesian inference, expected utility, temporal models and sequential decisions complement deterministic business optimisation.
Constrained search, linear/discrete optimisation and evaluated implementations directly support quantitative decisions.
R importing, cleaning, joining, visualisation and a data project support market and organisational evidence workflows.
Regression, classification, validation and predictor evaluation support statistical market inquiry; no business dataset is guaranteed.
Python programming, structured data, testing and computational problem solving support reproducible business-data methods.
Calculus, optimisation, differential equations and model implementation provide quantitative foundations, without claiming the complete vector/matrix curriculum.
Probability, inference, likelihood and sampling-algorithm analysis support uncertainty and statistical reasoning.
Institutions, markets, civil society, food/energy cases and policy advice support sustainability governance around firms and consumers.
Planetary boundaries, physical/chemical processes and material tests provide environmental understanding for product-impact claims.
Climate science, production and transport impacts, mitigation and stakeholder inquiry provide evidence for business climate responses.
Environmental/social/health impacts, costs and complete life-cycle assessment directly evaluate circular product and process choices.
Interviews, focus groups, research design, coding and executed qualitative inquiry support consumer and organisational research.
Description-supported environmental justice, social movements and case analysis explain contested transitions around firms and consumption.
Social cognition, influence, persuasion, group processes and research appraisal supply actual psychological foundations for consumer behaviour.
Framing, persuasion and actual circular-lifestyle communication projects connect consumer influence to sustainable behaviour.
blocks: Both study managerial accounting, costs, budgeting and financial reports. WUR develops allocation, variances and transfer pricing in greater depth; UCR also teaches investment appraisal.
Both study contract and commercial interactions. UCR emphasises cross-border transactions; WUR includes domestic corporate, liability, competition and consumer law.
Both examine preferences, strategic interaction and economic models. WUR introduces a broader evidence-led economics approach; UCR develops more extensive microeconomic analysis.
Both develop customer needs, new products and value creation. UCR centres a product-design process; WUR combines these with broader management and marketing.
Both apply marketing and strategic analysis to firms and consumers. WUR additionally develops broader management strategy and implementation.
Both examine strategic change and innovation in organisations. UCR emphasises digital transformation; WUR uses broader organisational-change cases.
Both execute consumer research to inform product decisions. WUR integrates social and natural sciences in a commissioned food-product concept; UCR provides broader market research.
Both introduce businesses, consumer needs and practical inquiry. WUR centres sustainable agri-food chains and academic study; UCR develops a startup business plan.
Both develop feasible research questions and designs. UCR also conducts empirical research and introduces statistics; WUR centres a research proposal.
Both address utility, uncertainty and decision analysis. UCR includes Bayesian and sequential agent models; WUR also develops multi-criteria methods and simulation.
Both study constrained, linear and discrete optimisation. UCR frames these as intelligent-agent methods; WUR includes production and business decision models.
Both develop applied mathematical analysis with software. WUR also explicitly includes vector and matrix algebra; the UCR course does not supply that whole combination.
Both address probability, distributions and inference. UCR has a more extensive mathematical-statistics and sampling component.
Both develop qualitative research through evidence collection and analysis. WUR also includes quantitative techniques; this is partial correspondence.
Both examine social influence, attitudes and psychological accounts of behaviour. WUR integrates these with economics, sociology and marketing specifically for consumption.
Further business foundations, choices and research

selection.assessment: Three provisional, substantively different concepts remain viable against current UCR content. The first strengthens quantitative decisions without claiming dedicated supply-chain study; the second adds actual social psychology, persuasion and qualitative research; the third integrates product/market study with life-cycle and governance evidence rather than laboratory recovery as business training. All pairwise floors pass. Business intelligence is already integrated in the closest core. The external thesis-guide condition blocks final comparison approval.

notes.text: WUR integrates firms and consumers around food, products and value chains, with named Business and Consumer majors and compulsory individual research. UCR offers substantial business, consumer, data and sustainability study, but does not reproduce the dedicated food-quality, sensory-science, supply-chain and complete decision-science sequence. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.
